background: ING Groep is the holding company of the Netherlands' largest bank, a digital-first retail and wholesale bank funded by deposits across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and other European markets, lending on mortgages and to corporates worldwide.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the group, at A on average and the weakest of them at A-, both on a stable outlook; neither has moved since a one-notch upgrade by one of them on 14 Apr 2016. The ratios are the weak part: CET1 of 13.1%, leverage of 4.2% and LCR of 137% are all in the bottom quarter of peers, with only NSFR of 128% above the median. Little has shifted — NSFR down 5 points since 30 Jun 2025, the rest broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged item, on 2 Sep 2026, is an Australian regulator raising capital requirements at the local unit after it overstated liquidity, which is the one to follow; the rest are strong first-half results.
